text.p: Ian Woosnam exorcised his three-month-old demon of Dubai with his victory in the British PGA Championship on Monday.
The 39-year-old Welshman thought of his fluffed chip at the last hole at Dubai in March as he played the last hole at Wentworth.
His bungled pitch into the lake there cost him the Desert Classic title when he had it all but sewn up.
But he came safely through the tall trees on the final hole on Monday despite some indecision on the tee that led to a hooked drive into the rough.
He holed the par five 18th to emerge with his first victory of the year and his second British PGA title after winning the event in 1988.
He beat a powerful field, leading for the last three rounds as he won by two strokes from a trio comprising Ryder Cup team mate Nick Faldo, South African Ernie Els and Irishman Darren Clarke.
Relatively pain-free from his perennially sore back, Woosnam immediately set new targets including winning the Order of Merit he previously headed in 1987 and 1990.
His prize of 183,340 pounds ($300,000) took him to the head of the 1997 list.
"And I would like to win the (British) Open. I would like to be in contention there again. I have not been in contention for several years."
He has never won the British Open, his only major title coming at the 1991 U.S. Masters.
"I'd like to win another major but it's nice to be winning tournaments again coming up to 40.
"With my back, there were times when I wondered if I would. But it has been feeling better in the last few weeks. I hope it stays like that."
Woosnam, who won four tournaments last year to finish second to Colin Montgomerie on the Order of Merit, took a one-stroke lead over Clarke into the final round.
But after pars on the first 11 holes, he was one behind the burly Irishman.
Then he birdied the 12th from 12 feet, Clarke bogeyed the 13th and Woosnam rolled in a 25-footer for birdie at 14. His one-shot deficit had become a two-stroke advantage.
Both players birdied the 571-yard 17th and when Clarke drove into a bunker at the last in an attempt to set up the eagle he needed to force a playoff, it was all but over.
When his second hit the lip of the bunker coming out, Woosnam could have won with a bogey but both players managed par and Woosnam was the winner.
"It was good playing under that pressure. I felt it and I managed to come through at the end," Woosnam said.
"Wentworth does bring out the best in the best players. You need experience on this golf course and I think that was my strength at the end."
